A 30-year-old woman presented with a 15-year history of recurrent ankle swelling and intermittent painful and tender nodules on her legs and feet. Her symptoms worsened during two pregnancies, which were carried to term. One and a half years before admission, she experienced escalation of symptoms, with nodules progressing to painful leg ulcers, and developed intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations. Previous treatments included wound care, leg compression, systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin, and rivaroxaban.
Patient had large, extremely tender, irregularly shaped circumferential leg ulcers, with violaceous and purpuric borders, areas of eschar, and a fibrinous base. Reticulated erythema and purpura were present on hands. Faintly erythematous, blanching macules and papules coalescing into patches and thin plaques were observed on bilateral thighs. Genital and oral ulcers were also present.
